BE IT HEREBY ORDAINED by the Mayor and Council of the/Town of Pine

Mountain, Georgia that conditions which are dangerous and injurious to the health, safety, and welfare of the people of the Town of Pine Mountain have been found to exist within the Town limits, those cnditions inciuding but not limited to dwellings, buildings, and other structures which are unsafe and unfit for human habitation and lands whose condition is unssfe or unsanitary.

Because these conditions have been found, a public necessity exists for their repair, closing, demolition, clearing, or cleaning.

The Mayor and Council of the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia, therefore ordain that ordinances which address these problems and provide a mechanism for their removal shall be adopted.

This _8th day of _NOVEMBER, 19933.

It is hereby declared by the Mayor and Council of the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia that under its police power and under authority granted to municipalities in #41-2-7 et seq. of the Official

Code of Georgia Annotated it is hereby ordained that the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia, shall and does have the authority to require repair of or to close or demolish dwellings, buildings, or structures of any sort which are determined to be, under the standards set forth herein, unfit, unsafe, dangerous or injurious to the health safety, and welfare of the people of the Town and the authority to require the cleaning or clearing of lands whose condition is determined to be, under the standards set forth herein, unsafe, dangerous, or injurious to the health, safety, and welfare of the people of the town.

SECTION I As used in this ordinance the following definitions apply:

A. "Public Authority” means the Chief of Police of the Town of Pine Mountain, the Superintendent of Public Works of the Town of Pine Mountain, the Building Inspector of Harris County, Georgia and/or the Chief Sanitation Officer of Harris County, Georgia and any agent appointed for purposes delineated within this ordinance by any of the four public officers named above.

B. "Public Officer" means the superintendent of public works of the Town of Pine Mountain or any agent appointed by him to exercise the powers delineated in this Ordinance.

Cc. "Drug crime™ means an act which is a violation of
3:
Controlled Substances Act.”

DB. "Dwellings, buildings or structures” means any building or structure or part thereof used and occupied for human habitation or commercial, industrial, or business uses, or intended to be so used and includes any outhouses and appurtenances belonging there to.

Also included is any building or structure of any sort or design.

E. "Owner" means the holder of the title in fee simple and every mortgagee of record.

F. "Parties in interest” means those persons in possession of the property and all other entities who have any interest of record in the property, including executors,

administrators, guardians, and trustees.

SECTION II: The Public Officer may determine that a dwelling, building, or structure, or lands within the town limits of the Town of Pine Mountain are unsafe, dangerous, or injurious to the public welfare if any of the following conditions exist at or on the structure or the land:

A. Any means of eqress or portion thereof is not of adequate size or is not arranged to provide a safe path of travel in case of fire or panic.

B. Any means of egress or portion thereof, such as but not limited to fire doors, closing devices and fire resistive ratings, is in disrepair or in a dilapidated or nonworking condition such that the means of egress could be rendered unsafe in case of fire or panic.

Cc. The stress in any material, member or portion thereof, due to all imposed loads including dead Load exceeds the stresses allowed in the Standard Building code for new buildings.

D. The building, structure or portion thereof has been damaged by fire, water, earthquake, wind or other cause to the extent that the structural integrity of the building or structure is less than it was prior to the damage and is less than the minimum requirement established by the Standard Building Code presentiy in effect in the State of Georgia as found in Titie 8 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated.

E, Any exterior appendage or portion of the building or structure is not securely Fastened, attached or anchored such that it is capable of resisting wind, seismic or similar loads as required hy the Standard Building code presentiy in effect in the State of Georgia as found in Title 8 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated.

F. If for any reason the building. structure or portion thereof is manifestly unsafe or unsanitary for the purpose for which it is being used.

Gc, The building, structure or portion thereof as a result of decay, deterioration or dilapidation is likely to fully or partially collapse.

H. The building, structure or portion thereof has been constructed or maintained in violation of a specific requirement of the Standard Code presently in effect in the State of Georgia as found in Title 8 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated.

I. Any building, structure or portion thereof that is in such a condition as to constitute a public nuisance.

J. Any building, structure or portion thereof that is unsafe, unsanitary or not provided with adequate egress, or which constitutes a fire hazard, or is otherwise dangerous to human life, or, which in relation to existing use, constitutes a hazard to safety or health by reason of inadequate maintenance, dilapidation, ebsolescence or abandonment.

K. The property in question is overgrown with weeds and brush and/or has stagnant water standing so as to provide a breeding place for pests and vermin.

a> The property is littered with refuse to include waste, rubbish, garbage, trash and other deleterious materials. The property has on or about it junk, lumber, debris, abandoned, discarded and unused objects such as appliances, furniture, barrels, tires, vehicles, and the like.

Further, the public officer may determine that as dwelling, building, or structure is vacant, dilapidated, and being used in connection with a commission of drug crimes upon personal observation and/or report of any law enforcement officer of any jurisdiction and upon presentation af evidence of drug crimes being committed at or on the property.

SECTION III The procedure to be observed to determine if an unfit, unsafe, or dangerous condition exists is as follows:

A request shall be made for an investigation of a specified condition by public suthority, by at least five (5) residents of the Town of Pine Mountain, those residents heing required to reside in the Town of Pine Mountain on or before the date on which the alleged dangerous or unsafe condition arose, or an investigation shall be initiated on his own motion by the public officer.

After the initiation of the request, which shall be in writing, although no particular format shall be required, the public officer shall make a preliminary investigation of the condition. The public officer is authorized to enter upon the property for making a preliminary investigation; he shall do so in such a Manner as to create the least possibie inconvenience to the persons in possession.

If he determines that the request for an investigation has a basis in fact under the standards set forth in this ordinance, then he Shall cause to be issued and served upon the owner and the parties in interest of the property a complaint.

The complaint shall state the nature of the request made initially as well as the facts determined under his preliminary

investigation.

In addition, the complaint shali set forth a hearing date, tine, and place, with the to be not less than ten (10) days nor more than thirty (30) days after service of the complaint.

The owner and/or any parties in interest may, but are not required to, file a written answer to the complaint.

Service of the complaint shail be made in accordance with # 41-2-12 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, including the filing of a copy of the complaint in the 1is pendens docket of the Clerk of Superior Court of Harris County, Georgia.
4:
A hearing shall be conducted in the Municipal Court of the Town, and the judge shall have the power in said hearing to administer oaths and affirmations, to examine witnesses, and to receive evidence; however, the rules of evidence prevailing in courts of law or the owner and all parties in interest who wish to be heard shall be given an opportunity to testify and to call witnesses.

The Judge may question witnesses and may call additional witnesses on his own notion, inciuding any law enforcement officers of any jurisdiction, or the buiiding inspector of Harris County, Georgia, or the Chief Sanitation officer of Harris County, Georgia.
5:
The Court Shall, after the hearing is concluded, determine if conditions exist which create an unsafe, unfit or injurious circumstance for the public welfare. Tf such a finding is made, the Judge shall state in writing his Findings of fact and shall issue an order to the owner of the property and shall cause such order to be served upon the owner.

If the repair, improvement, or remedying of the dangerous, unfit or injurious conditions can be made at a reasonable cost in relation to the value of the property, the order shall require that the owner, within sixty days from the date of the order, repair or remedy the condition found to exist s0 as to render it no longer unfit, unsafe, or injuricus to the public welfare.

If the repair or remedying of the condition cannot be made at a reasonable cost relative to the value of the property, the order shall require that the owner, within sixty days, remove or demolish any dwelling, buiiding or structure; provided, hawever, that no such removal or demolition ghali be required unless there is a specific finding that the cost of remedying or repairing will exceed one-half the value of the property after repair.

If the owner fails to comply with an order to remove or demolish, the public officer may cause such removal or demolition. If public removal or demolition is ordered, there shall be posted

on the main entrance of any buiiding, dwelling or structure the following side:

"This Building is unfit for human habitation or commercial, industrial, or business use; the use or occupation of this building for human habitation or for commercial, industrial, or business use is prohibited and unlawful.”

Provided, however, that no public removal or demolition of any property shall be accomplished unless the Mayor and Council of the Town of Pine Mountain Shell by ordinance have ordered the public officer to proceed in regard ta the particular property affected.
6:
If public removal or demolition is carried out, then the cost of such removal or demolition shall be lien against the real property and shall attach to the real property upon the filing of an itemized statement of the total sum of public cost paid for the removal or demolition in the office of the Clerk of the Superior Court of Harris County, Georgia on the general execution docket.

Provided if there are saleable materials left from the removal or demolition of the property, they shail be sold at public sale and any proceeds shali be credited against the cost of the removal and any balance shall be deposited in the Superior Court by the public officer to be disbursed by order of the court.

fhe collection of amounts due from the owner pursuant to the lien aS recorded shall proceed as set forth in Official Code of Georgia Annotated # 41-2=9(7).

SECTION VII Nothing in this Ordinance shall be construed a abrogating or impairing the rights of private individuals or the public to petition the appropriate court for the abatement of a public or private nuisance.

SECTION VIII If any portion of this ordinance shall for any reason be adjudged by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, for any reason, such judgment shall not affect, impair, or invalidate the remainder of the ordinance.
